current_repo_state.b_origin: 岬端 (ポントゥケシ) [NeckeRechtstûr] — Calque: Maritime cape + Upright integrity

b_pogibi.first_mention_attestation: Attested c. 1810 CE as Pokobē (ポコベー) in Mamiya Rinzō's Kita Ezo-shima Chizu (Map of Northern Ezo Island) following his 1808–1809 CE Sakhalin survey.
b_pogibi.etymology_analysis: From Nivkh Pokobi / Pogibi, the indigenous name of Cape Pogibi at the narrowest point of the Nevelskoy Strait in northwestern Sakhalin (rendered Hokobei / 鉾部 in Japanese). First recorded in written cartography c. 1810 CE, long after 867 CE.

current_repo_state.name: WeitJamatoVaste
current_repo_state.b_origin: 博和必 (ポギビ) [WeitJamatoVaste] — Calque: Broad learning + Harmony + Certain

b_tym_sakhalin.first_mention_attestation: Attested in 1852 CE in Lieutenant N. K. Boshnyak's expedition report to Gennady Nevelskoy documenting the Tym River (Тымь) and its Nivkh settlements.
b_tym_sakhalin.etymology_analysis: From Nivkh Tymy ('spawning ground', adapted into Russian as Tym' and Ainu as Tuymi), directly adopting the hydronym of the Tym River in central-northern Sakhalin. Unattested in written records until 1852 CE, well after 867 CE.

current_repo_state.name: BêstRîs
current_repo_state.b_origin: 特米 (トゥイミ) [BêstRîs] — Calque: Exceptional preeminence + Polished grain rice

b_idoi.first_mention_attestation: Attested c. 1810 CE as Idoi (イドイ) in Mamiya Rinzō's Kita Ezo-shima Chizu (Map of Northern Ezo Island), corresponding to the Otchishi / Doe settlement (modern Aleksandrovsk-Sakhalinsky).
b_idoi.etymology_analysis: Japanese cartographic rendering Idoi (イドイ) of the indigenous Ainu/Nivkh settlement at modern Aleksandrovsk-Sakhalinsky (also known as Otchishi or Nivkh Doe). First attested in Mamiya Rinzō's c. 1810 CE map, post-dating 867 CE.

current_repo_state.name: Sîdenbrunn
current_repo_state.b_origin: 丝井 (イドイ) [Sîdenbrunn] — Calque: Silk thread + Well

b_tarayka.first_mention_attestation: Attested c. 1810–1811 CE in Mamiya Rinzō's Kita Ezo-shima Chizu and Hokui Bunkai Yowa as Tarayka (タライカ / 多来加) on the Gulf of Patience.

morphemes.translation: indigenous ethnonym and settlement name on Patience Bay

b_tarayka.etymology_analysis: From Tarayka (Japanese 多来加), the indigenous name of the eastern Sakhalin settlement and Ainu/Uilta/Nivkh contact zone near Lake Taraika (Nevskoye) and Poronaysk. First documented in Japanese surveys c. 1810 CE, post-dating 867 CE.

current_repo_state.name: MênichKomKâ
current_repo_state.b_origin: 多来加 (タライカ) [MênichKomKâ] — Calque: Abundant + Arrival + Augment

b_eusutur.first_mention_attestation: Attested in 1905 CE (Meiji 38) with the Japanese settlement and administrative naming of Esutoru (恵須取, modern Uglegorsk) in Karafuto.

morphemes.translation: indigenous coastal place name (exact gloss uncertain)

b_eusutur.etymology_analysis: From Sakhalin Ainu Esturi (adapted into Japanese as Esutoru / 恵須取, modern Uglegorsk), whose precise lexical meaning is unconfirmed. Unattested in written records until 1905 CE, long after 867 CE.

current_repo_state.name: Houbtberch
current_repo_state.b_origin: 头山 (エストゥル) [Houbtberch] — Calque: Headland + Mountain

b_ketuni.first_mention_attestation: Attested in 1917 CE in the Karafuto Hōrei Ruiju (樺太法令類聚) as Keton (気屯) within Shisuka District.
b_ketuni.etymology_analysis: From Nivkh Ketongiy ('upper river', referring to the Keton River tributary of the Poronai, rendered in Japanese as Keton / 気屯, modern Smirnykh). Unattested in written sources until 1917 CE, post-dating 867 CE.

current_repo_state.name: OuweBou
current_repo_state.b_origin: 岸築 (ケトゥニ) [OuweBou] — Calque: Riparian riverbank + Fortified earthwork

b_ioci.first_mention_attestation: Attested in 1646 CE (Shōhō 3) in Matsumae Kagehiro's Shinra no Kiroku as Yoichi (與依地 / 余市), marking the western limit of Wajin-Ainu coastal contact.
b_ioci.etymology_analysis: Commonly derived from Ainu i-ot-i ('place where [snakes] are many', using the taboo word i for snake), or i-o-ci ('place where hot springs flow into the river'). First attested in Shinra no Kiroku in 1646 CE, post-dating 867 CE.

current_repo_state.name: KomRastLêg
current_repo_state.b_origin: 来止卧 (イオチ) [KomRastLêg] — Calque: Arrival + Stationary boundary post + Recumbent

b_setanay.first_mention_attestation: Attested in 1646 CE (Shōhō 3) in Matsumae Kagehiro's Shinra no Kiroku, which records the 16th-century Ainu chieftain Hashitain of Setanai (瀬田内 / 瀬棚).
b_setanay.etymology_analysis: From Ainu seta-nay ('dog river', shortened from seta-rupespe-nay, 'river that dogs swim across'). First attested in written records in 1646 CE (Shinra no Kiroku), well after 867 CE.

current_repo_state.name: Snellbachbache
current_repo_state.b_origin: 濑川 (セタナイ) [Snellbachbache] — Calque: Shallow rapids + Flowing stream

b_otarunay.first_mention_attestation: Attested in 1700 CE (Genroku 13) in the Matsumae-jima Gōchō (松前島郷帳) submitted by the Matsumae Domain to the Tokugawa shogunate.
b_otarunay.etymology_analysis: From Ainu ota-or-un-nay ('river running through the sandy beach'), later shortened to Otaru (小樽). First attested in written records in 1700 CE (Matsumae-jima Gōchō), post-dating 867 CE.

current_repo_state.name: Santbache
current_repo_state.b_origin: 砂川 (オタルナイ) [Santbache] — Calque: Sand + Flowing stream

b_aptapet_ainu.first_mention_attestation: Attested in 1700 CE (Genroku 13) in the Matsumae-jima Gōchō as Abuta (あふた), derived from the Ainu name Aptapet.
b_aptapet_ainu.etymology_analysis: From Ainu apta-pet ('river where fishhooks were made and used for fishing'), modern Abuta (虻田). First attested in written records in 1700 CE (Matsumae-jima Gōchō), post-dating 867 CE.

b_iskar_hokkaido.first_mention_attestation: Attested in 1644 CE (Shōhō 1) on the Shōhō Okuniezu (正保御国絵図) and in 1700 CE in the Matsumae-jima Gōchō as Ishikari (いしかり).
b_iskar_hokkaido.etymology_analysis: From Ainu Iskar-pet ('winding river' or 'beautifully made river'), directly adopting the hydronym of the Ishikari River (石狩川). First attested in written cartography in 1644 CE, post-dating 867 CE.

current_repo_state.name: Krûmmebache
current_repo_state.b_origin: 曲川 (イシカラ) [Krûmmebache] — Calque: Winding river bend + Flowing stream

b_rurmo_otpe.first_mention_attestation: Attested in 1661 CE (Kanbun 1) on a domain map as Tsuruotsube (つるをつへ) and in 1700 CE in the Matsumae-jima Gōchō, reflecting Ainu Rur-mo-ot-pe (modern Rumoi).
b_rurmo_otpe.etymology_analysis: From Ainu rur-mo-ot-pe ('river with calm, constant tides'), directly adopting the hydronym of the Rumoi River (留萌川). First attested in written records in 1661 CE, post-dating 867 CE.

current_repo_state.name: Sachtleiteflôz
current_repo_state.b_origin: 缓坂流 (ルルモオッペ) [Sachtleiteflôz] — Calque: Gentle slope + Mountain slope + Flowing current

b_cup_pet.first_mention_attestation: Attested in 1797 CE (Kansei 9) in Matsumae retainer Takahashi Hiromitsu's Matsumae-chi narabini Tōzai Ezo-chi Meisaiki as Chikubetsu (チクベツ / 忠別川).
b_cup_pet.etymology_analysis: From Ainu Cup-pet ('sun river' or 'eastern river', also interpreted as ci-up-pet 'river with waves'), directly adopting the hydronym of the Chūbetsu River (忠別川) in Asahikawa. First attested in written records in 1797 CE, post-dating 867 CE.

current_repo_state.name: TrûweScheid
current_repo_state.b_origin: 忠别 (チュプペッ) [TrûweScheid] — Calque: Loyalty + Branch river

b_sorapci.first_mention_attestation: Attested in 1859 CE (Ansei 6) in Matsuura Takeshirō's Tōzai Ezo Sansen Chiri Torishirabe-zu (東西蝦夷山川地理取調図) as Sorapuchi (ソラプチ / 空知川).
b_sorapci.etymology_analysis: From Ainu so-rap-ci ('cascading waterfalls'), directly adopting the hydronym of the Sorachi River (空知川). First attested in written surveys in 1859 CE by Matsuura Takeshirō, long after 867 CE.

current_repo_state.name: Kleinval
current_repo_state.b_origin: 小泷 (ソラプチ) [Kleinval] — Calque: Little + Rushing waterfall rapids

b_sar.first_mention_attestation: Attested in 1700 CE (Genroku 13) in the Matsumae-jima Gōchō (松前島郷帳) as Saru (さる).
b_sar.etymology_analysis: From Ainu sar ('reed plain / marshland'), referring to the lower Saru River (沙流川) valley in Hidaka. First attested in written records in 1700 CE (Matsumae-jima Gōchō), post-dating 867 CE.

current_repo_state.name: Rietveit
current_repo_state.b_origin: 苇原 (サル) [Rietveit] — Calque: Reed + High plateau plain

b_iput.first_mention_attestation: Attested in 1700 CE (Genroku 13) in the Matsumae-jima Gōchō (松前島郷帳) in the entry 'Ishikari yori Ifutsu Ezo kyosho' (いしかりよりいふつ蝦夷居所).
b_iput.etymology_analysis: From Ainu i-put ('entrance/river mouth leading to an important place'), referring to the confluence area near modern Ebetsu (江別). First attested in written records in 1700 CE (Matsumae-jima Gōchō), post-dating 867 CE.

current_repo_state.name: BacheZâmenstat
current_repo_state.b_origin: 川合所 (イプッ) [BacheZâmenstat] — Calque: Flowing stream + Confluence + Place

b_sipicar.first_mention_attestation: Attested in 1669 CE (Kanbun 9) in Tokugawa shogunate, Matsumae, and Tsugaru records of Shakushain's Revolt as Shibuchari / Shibechari (シブチャリ / シベチャリ).
b_sipicar.etymology_analysis: From Ainu sipe-ican / sipe-icar ('salmon spawning ground'), directly adopting the historical hydronym of the Shibechari River (modern Shizunai River). First attested in written records in 1669 CE during Shakushain's Revolt, post-dating 867 CE.

current_repo_state.name: Grôzsteinveitlant
current_repo_state.b_origin: 大石原地 (シピチャリ) [Grôzsteinveitlant] — Calque: Great + Stone + High plateau plain + Land

b_moruran.first_mention_attestation: Attested in late 16th-century Matsumae trading-post accounts and documented in 1700 CE (Genroku 13) in the Matsumae-jima Gōchō as Mororan / Moruran (Muroran).
b_moruran.etymology_analysis: From Ainu mo-ruerani ('bottom of a little slope'), modern Muroran (室蘭). Unattested in written records until the late 16th–1700 CE Matsumae period, well after 867 CE.

current_repo_state.name: KleinNiderleite
current_repo_state.b_origin: 小下坂 (モルラン) [KleinNiderleite] — Calque: Little + Lower + Mountain slope

b_matomai.first_mention_attestation: Attested in 1356 CE (Enbun 1) in the Suwa Daimyōjin Ekotoba (諏訪大明神絵詞) as Matōmainu (万堂宇満伊犬), identified as the early Wajin-Ainu port of Matsumae.
b_matomai.etymology_analysis: From Ainu mat-oma-i ('place where women live' or 'place in front of the cove/bay'), rendered in Japanese as Matsumae (松前). First attested in 1356 CE in the Suwa Daimyōjin Ekotoba, post-dating 867 CE.

current_repo_state.name: PînVör
current_repo_state.b_origin: 松前 (マトマイ) [PînVör] — Calque: Pine tree + Front

b_uskes.first_mention_attestation: Attested in 1356 CE (Enbun 1) in the Suwa Daimyōjin Ekotoba (諏訪大明神絵詞) as Usorikeshi (宇曽利鶴子), and later as Usukeshi (宇須岸) in Shinra no Kiroku (modern Hakodate).
b_uskes.etymology_analysis: From Ainu usor-kes / us-kes ('end of the bay'), an Ainu locator compound for the fishing settlement at modern Hakodate (函館). First attested in 1356 CE in the Suwa Daimyōjin Ekotoba, post-dating 867 CE.

current_repo_state.name: BuchtRechtstûr
current_repo_state.b_origin: 湾端 (ウスケシ) [BuchtRechtstûr] — Calque: Coastal gulf bay + Upright integrity

b_kayaunpesh.first_mention_attestation: Attested in 1700 CE (Genroku 13) in Edo-period Matsumae records as Kayabe (茅部), derived from Ainu Kaya-un-pe / Kaya-un-pes.
b_kayaunpesh.etymology_analysis: From Ainu kaya-un-pes ('cliff with sails', referring to sail-shaped coastal rock formations in Kayabe, southern Oshima Peninsula). Unattested in written records until the Edo period (c. 1700 CE), post-dating 867 CE.

current_repo_state.name: Segelklif
current_repo_state.b_origin: 帆崖 (カヤウンペシ) [Segelklif] — Calque: Sail + Precipitous rock cliff

b_kumausi.first_mention_attestation: Attested in early 17th-century Matsumae records (1615 CE / Genna 1 foundation of Ainuma Hachiman Shrine and 1616 CE legend of Kigan Kumaishi) as Kumaishi (熊石).
b_kumausi.etymology_analysis: From Ainu kuma-us-i ('place with many fish-drying racks'), located at the historical northern boundary of Wajinchi in Oshima/Hiyama (modern Yakumo). First attested in early 17th-century Matsumae records (1615 CE), post-dating 867 CE.

current_repo_state.name: Bêrenstein
current_repo_state.b_origin: 熊石 (クマウシ) [Bêrenstein] — Calque: Bear + Stone
